en: 1. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the Dharmadhātugarbha, within the range of the Tathāgatas, in the Infinite Array, together with a great community of monks. Now at that time, a girl named Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitā had gathered and was seated in that very assembly.

2. Then the maiden Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitā addressed the Blessed One as follows: “Blessed One, who are the non-virtuous friends of a bodhisattva, with whom a bodhisattva mahāsattva should not dwell even for a single night? The Blessed One said:

"Daughter, I do not perceive any unwholesome friends for a bodhisattva mahāsattva in this world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, except for those who belong to the vehicle of the śrāvakas—those beginners who have first resolved their minds upon the Mahāyāna; daughter, these are the unwholesome friends of a bodhisattva."

3. For what reason? Because he has set out for his own welfare, a bodhisattva who is a beginner with the first production of the thought of awakening should not dwell in the same monastery or the same cell as those belonging to the vehicle of the śrāvakas in the Mahāyāna; nor should he walk on the same walking-path, nor even travel along the same road.

4. Otherwise, I permit that a bodhisattva who is learned (*bahuśruta*) and endowed with unshakable faith should dwell together with them for the sake of ripening [others] in the Mahāyāna and for the sake of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttarā samyaksambodhi*). However, such sūtras must not be revealed to beings whose roots of virtue (*kuśalamūla*) are not yet matured. Why is that? Because these [sūtras] are detrimental to the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*); they cause one to become disenchanted with the thought of awakening; they cause harm to the thought of awakening.

5. "Indeed, daughter, it is better for a bodhisattva to give up his own life than to ever abandon the thought of awakening (bodhicitta) by attending to the mental orientations associated with the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. Furthermore, daughter, if that bodhisattva, having abandoned the thought of awakening and addressed all sentient beings, should produce another thought—namely, that of the level of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas—and if they were to harm or discourage the thought of awakening of a bodhisattva, both of these [actions] would result in no opportunity [for liberation]."

6. "Daughter, it is better for a bodhisattva to have committed actions associated with the five deeds of immediate retribution than to cultivate the fruit of stream-entry while devoid of the thought of awakening. For it is better, daughter, for a bodhisattva who is embraced by the thought of awakening to dwell in hell for an eon or a thousand eons, than for one devoid of the thought of awakening to cultivate the fruit of once-returning."

7. "Indeed, daughter, it is better for a bodhisattva to be reborn among the animals than for one devoid of the thought of awakening (bodhicitta) to cultivate the fruit of a non-returner (anāgāmiphala). Indeed, daughter, it is better for a bodhisattva to commit the taking of life and dwell in hell than, being devoid of the thought of awakening, to realize arhatship and enter final nirvana like a cowardly thief.

Indeed, daughter, it is better for a bodhisattva with a mind embraced by all sentient beings to desire even a pit of fire than for one devoid of the thought of awakening to dwell in the nirvana of a śrāvaka."

8. O girl, by the production of the thought of awakening which is embraced by all sentient beings, one becomes worthy of worship and an object of veneration for the world with its gods, humans, and asuras; one surpasses all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; and Māra, his mind agitated, is rendered humbled, as are the hosts of Māra’s followers.

9. When this had been said, the maiden Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitā addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, who are to be known as belonging to the host of Māra? The Blessed One replied: "Daughter, those who, when this very Mahāyāna is being spoken, taught, proclaimed, or recited, do not hear it, do not master it, do not have faith in it, but instead mock it, deride it, and speak its dispraise—they are to be known as belonging to the host of Māra."
They should be known as unrighteous persons; they should be known as followers of other sects; they should be known as those who have entered upon a false path.

Having rejected the Mahāyāna, they will indeed be reborn in the Avīci great hell. When they pass away from there, they will be reborn among those who consume urine and excrement, and for immeasurable eons they will subsist on such things. Even if they should at some time attain human birth, they will then be blind, mute, deaf, deformed in limb, and flat-nosed.
Thereafter, in due succession, they will come into meeting with the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, throughout the world-systems of the ten directions.

From those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, speech issues forth individually—whether associated with the vehicle of the disciples (*śrāvakayāna*), the vehicle of the solitary buddhas (*pratyekabuddhayāna*), or the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*). Nevertheless, through their effortless spontaneity (*anābhoga*), from every single pore of the skin of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, there issue forth many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of light-rays of Dharma, by means of the utterance of a single sound.

12. Therein, those beings gathered in the assembly who were inclined toward the Śrāvaka vehicle heard the Śrāvaka vehicle issuing from the mouth of the Tathāgata; those beings who were inclined toward the Pratyekabuddha vehicle heard the Pratyekabuddha vehicle issuing from the mouth of the Tathāgata; and those beings who were inclined toward the Mahāyāna heard the Mahāyāna issuing from the mouth of the Tathāgata.

Even sentient beings belonging to the animal realm hear [the teaching] through their own respective loud cries. Therein, those sentient beings who have not previously heard the word of the Buddha see the Tathāgata having become silent. Among them, those sentient beings who reject the Mahāyāna will experience the sufferings of the hells, animals, hungry ghosts, and the world of Yama for many eons, after which they will gain faith in the Mahāyāna and give rise to the resolve for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
(Note: This parallel idea appears in the *Acintyatathāgataguhyanirdeśa*!)

13. Then the maiden Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitā said this to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, when it is said ‘Mahāyāna, Mahāyāna,’ what is the referent of this designation? Then the Blessed One gave his approval to that maiden: “Excellent, excellent, maiden! Since you wish to hear the qualities and benefits of the Mahāyāna, listen then, maiden, and attend well and properly; I shall speak to you the designation of the Mahāyāna.”

14. 1) Furthermore, daughter, that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is vast and great; 2) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is immeasurable; 3) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is imperturbable; 4) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is inexhaustible; 5) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is of infinite extent; 6) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is like the ocean; 7) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is honored by *garuḍas*, *kinnaras*, and *mahoragas*; 8) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is sung of by *gandharvas*; 9) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is worshipped by the gods.

10) That vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is honored by Brahmā; 11) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is honored by the lords of the Daityas; 12) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is honored by Śakra, the lord of the gods; 13) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is embraced by all the nāgas; 14) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is practiced by the bodhisattvas; 15) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, sustains the lineage of the Buddhas; 16) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is worshipped by those of great renown.

17) That vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is the life-sustenance for all sentient beings; 18) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is like a medicinal tree; 19) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is the destroyer of all afflictions.

16.20) That vehicle, the Mahāyāna, follows the turning of the wheel of Dharma; 21) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is inexpressible; 22) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, ensures the non-interruption of the lineage of the Three Jewels; 23) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is not antagonistic toward those beings whose inclinations are inferior or timid; 24) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, gives rise to Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas; 25) that vehicle, the Mahāyāna, is the supreme among all vehicles.

Furthermore, while this discourse on the qualities and benefits of the Mahāyāna was being spoken, this trichiliocosm shook in six ways. Hundreds of thousands of musical instruments, though unstruck, resounded in the sky, and showers of flowers rained down from the expanse of the heavens. Many hundreds of thousands of sons of gods conceived the aspiration for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, and the bodhisattvas who were beginners attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena.

18. Then the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what is the name of this Dharma-discourse, and how should I remember it? The Blessed One said: "Remember it as 'The Teaching on the Merits and Benefits of the Mahāyāna,' and remember it as 'The Teaching on the Obstruction of Karma from Rejecting the True Dharma. Thus spoke the Blessed One. The Venerable Ānanda, the girl Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitā, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken."
The Mahāyāna sūtra titled *The Questions of the Maiden Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitā*, the eighteenth, is completed.
